title: Artifact Knowledge Graph — Data Map
summary: Type-level map of leafcutter-ai's artifact nodes and the fields that connect them. Each edge carries the field that encodes it plus a two-axis trust rating (enforcement x shape), and a status marking whether the relation exists at all — relations the graph needs but the repo does not have are recorded as status 'absent' rather than omitted. This is the static schema of the knowledge graph; the dynamic Atlas view will later render live instances against these same edge types.

status.present: The relation exists in the repo and is encoded by the named field.
status.absent: The relation does NOT exist. Recorded deliberately so a missing traversal is distinguishable from one that was never needed. Carries no encoding field and is always enforcement 'none'.

enforcement.enforced: A pre-commit hook and/or required CI gate blocks violations.
enforcement.derived-validated: Machine-generated AND its freshness/parity is blocked at commit.

shape.clean: Single unambiguous value form; ingestable as-is.
shape.ambiguous: One field multiplexes several edge types; must be partitioned.
shape.often-empty: Frequently blank in the live store.

legend.ingestable_rule: A link is ingestable as-is only when status is 'present' AND enforcement is 'enforced' or 'derived-validated' AND shape is 'clean'. A status 'absent' edge is never ingestable — it documents a gap to be built.

GAP — answers 'given this file, which ACs govern it?'. No source file carries any marker naming the AC it implements, and no index inverts the relation. Today this must be reconstructed by inverting ac-impl-source (UNTRUSTED) or by joining Ticket.files_touched -> ac_traceability (warn-rated). This is the single most load-bearing missing edge for refactoring: it is what tells you what not to touch.

GAP — answers 'which tests guard this file?'. No coverage data is ingested into any artifact, so nothing records which source a test actually exercises. Only Test -> AC (test-covers) exists, so file-level test protection can only be guessed from import paths.

GAP — answers 'when was this AC shipped?'. Changelog entries carry components, adrs, commits and a free-text ticket basename, but never AC ids. The nearest proxies are AC.implemented_by (UNTRUSTED) and raw git history; neither yields a release date per AC.

GAP — answers 'which ACs does this screen realise?'. A mockup declares a screen id but carries no AC back-link. Derivable transitively by reversing flownode-renders and following flownode-implements, so this is a convenience gap rather than a data gap — but screen-level AC lookup requires a join through the flow.
